theme.title: Lakers lore
theme.subtitle: Minneapolis and Los Angeles
theme.recap: Long before Showtime the Lakers had Elgin Baylor's Finals record and a 1971–72 team that did not lose for two months.

questions.prompt: The 1971–72 Lakers set the NBA record for consecutive wins. How long was the streak?
questions.note: 33 in a row, an NBA record.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: they would also go on an NBA record 33-game winning streak

funFacts.text: Coach Bill Sharman replaced the Lakers' old habits with strict conditioning and an up-tempo fast break.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: He introduced strict conditioning drills and implemented a running fast break-based offense

funFacts.text: Wilt's job changed: rather than hunt shots, he rebounded and started fast breaks with quick outlet passes.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: focus on defense, rebounding, and jump-starting the fast break with quick outlet passes

funFacts.text: The transition style proved too demanding for the injured Elgin Baylor, whose retirement opened a starting job for Jim McMillian.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: He was replaced at small forward by Jim McMillian

questions.prompt: The 1971–72 Lakers set a regular-season wins record. What was their win total?
questions.note: 69–13, a record that stood until the 1995–96 Bulls.

funFacts.text: The defending champion Bucks, led by Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, were expected to own the league for years.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The defending champion Milwaukee Bucks, led by superstar Kareem Abdul-Jabbar

funFacts.text: Los Angeles swept Chicago in the conference semifinals before battling Milwaukee in the West finals.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Western Conference Semifinals: 4–0

funFacts.text: Boston had repeatedly denied the Lakers a championship after their move west, making this title particularly cathartic.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Lakers lost the championship to them six times in eight years

questions.prompt: By how many points per game did the 1971–72 Lakers outscore their opponents?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: outscoring opponents by 12.3 points per game in the regular season

funFacts.text: In March, Los Angeles put on a staggering scoring display in a home rout of Golden State.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: 78 March 19 Golden State 99–162 Gail Goodrich

funFacts.text: Gail Goodrich lit up Houston during a December road victory, leading the Lakers' attack.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: 27 December 8 @ Houston 125–120 Gail Goodrich (42)

funFacts.text: The club's home record was exceptional, but its road success was nearly as impressive.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote:
1971–72 game log
Total: 69–13 (Home: 36–5; Road: 33–8)

questions.prompt: In the game that clinched the 1972 title, Wilt Chamberlain had 24 points and how many rebounds?
questions.context: 1972 NBA Finals · Game 5 · vs New York
questions.note: 29 rebounds, and the Finals MVP award.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Wilt Chamberlain scored 24 points and 29 rebounds and earned the NBA Finals MVP Award

funFacts.text: Chamberlain was listed as doubtful for the clincher with a sprained right wrist, yet played anyway.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Chamberlain was listed as doubtful for Game Five with a sprained right wrist

funFacts.text: ABC announcer Keith Jackson informally tallied Wilt's blocks before the NBA officially tracked them.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: ABC announcer Keith Jackson counted them up during the broadcast

funFacts.text: The victory delivered the Lakers' first championship since the franchise relocated from Minneapolis.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: win their sixth NBA title and their first since 1954, when the team was still based in Minneapolis

questions.prompt: What is the NBA record for points in a Finals game, set by Elgin Baylor in 1962?
questions.context: Los Angeles Lakers vs Boston Celtics · 1962 NBA Finals

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Baylor set the still-standing NBA record for points in an NBA Finals game with 61.

funFacts.text: Baylor helped turn basketball into a vertical spectacle; later high-flying stars modeled their moves on his.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Baylor introduced a creative and acrobatic playing style that would later be emulated

funFacts.text: Seattle University eventually named its basketball court for Baylor, honoring the former college star.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: they named its basketball court in honor of him

funFacts.text: Although Baylor retired before the Lakers' breakthrough, the team presented him with a championship ring.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Lakers did give Baylor a championship ring for his contributions at the start of the 1971–72 season
